decisions.reason: The existing message-61 MODIFY already records the solenoid valve and controlled mix-then-open-then-pour component requirement in the BOM.
The candidate already requires the spout to be removable or simple to clean; the solenoid and dispensing-sequence change does not necessarily alter that requirement.
The no-leak and effective-seal language reiterates the existing leak-free plumbing requirement without changing its state.
Preventing leakage into the base is already represented by the liquid-isolation requirement, and the controlled-dispensing change introduces no new isolation rule.
Selecting a solenoid control mechanism does not change the spout's recorded location, orientation, material, access, or appearance.
The existing message-61 MODIFY already captures the little-to-no-splash target, optional guard or lip, and live-event context.
The solenoid dispensing decision does not necessarily change the established enclosure thickness, well depth, or overall size constraint.
The dispensing-control change has no effect on the beige body or green accent colors.
Message 61 does not revise the bowl capacity, depth, geometry, or enclosure-size constraint.
The existing quick-removal behavior already supports removable bowls, while the solenoid dispensing change does not alter swap speed or event-exchange behavior.
The dispensing sequence is intended to preserve texture but does not revise the candidate's mixing or foam outcomes; the same-message whisk uncertainty is already represented separately.
Adding solenoid-based dispensing does not logically entail changing the established standard 120V wall-power requirement.
